$comment: SYNAPSE -- committed thresholds for the Effectiveness_Baseline check (R8.10; design E6; AD-13).
Read by `frontend/spec/effectiveness/check-baseline.ts` (utf-8 on every read, E-S13-07) and
passed to `frontend/src/lib/effectiveness-baseline.ts::validateBaseline`. The validator holds no
numeric literal of its own: every number the authored-ceiling rule compares against lives here,
so the rule is reviewable and diffable rather than buried in TypeScript (AD-13).
THE RULE, R8.10 verbatim: 'IF every row carries an identical `steps` value and an identical
`latencyMs` value, THEN THE baseline check SHALL fail the baseline as an authored ceiling rather
than accept it as a measurement.' The conjunction is deliberate. Two Jobs-To-Be-Done may
honestly need the same number of affordance activations, so uniform `steps` alone is not the
tell; uniform `steps` AND uniform millisecond latencies across every row is, because a measured
time-to-complete does not repeat exactly across five different operator paths.
`min_distinct_steps` / `min_distinct_latency_ms` are the counts of DISTINCT values the row set
must exhibit. The baseline fails as an authored ceiling only when BOTH counts fall below their
minimum. Both are floored at 2 by the policy schema: a value of 1 would satisfy any single-
valued column and so would switch the rule off from configuration, which is exactly the
weakening this file exists to make visible.
`min_rows` is the row count below which the distinctness rule cannot be evaluated at all (one
row is trivially uniform in both columns). Below it the baseline is rejected as UNEVALUABLE, not
accepted: absence of proof is never a pass (I-7). It is NOT the declared Job_To_Be_Done count --
the row-to-job bijection is R8.1/R8.3, and its single source of truth is `JOB_ORDER` in
`frontend/src/lib/effectiveness-scorecard.ts`, never a number copied to here.
Seeded from the audit finding, not from a measurement. The committed
`frontend/spec/effectiveness/scorecard.baseline.json` carries `steps: 20` and `latencyMs: 15000`
on all five rows and carries no per-row capture stamps, so it FAILS this check as landed. That
failure is R8.10's finding becoming mechanical, not a defect in this file; it clears only when
the browser harness (task 11.1) and the complete-or-failed emitter (task 11.2) produce a
measured, per-row-stamped baseline.
